coverage: Limited pilot: three concern guides and selected City Council items. This is not a complete agenda or an address-based jurisdiction lookup.

topics.title: A crossing or street feels unsafe
topics.keywords: crosswalk traffic sidewalk bike road pedestrian
topics.authority: PBOT reviews non-urgent street-safety concerns. Some roads belong to ODOT or Multnomah County; ask the agency to confirm ownership for the exact location.
topics.process: Submit the location and concern through PBOT’s safety form. Staff review engineering standards and available funding. Larger projects can require separate Council authorization.
topics.action: Report a non-urgent concern to PBOT

topics.title: How does the city support affordable housing?
topics.keywords: rent affordable nonprofit tax exemption housing
topics.body: Portland Housing Bureau and City Council
topics.authority: The Housing Bureau administers the nonprofit low-income housing tax exemption. City Council decides changes to the city code that governs it.
topics.process: The bureau prepares a proposal; a Council committee can review it and refer it to the full Council. A committee recommendation is not final approval.

topics.title: My TriMet bus service is changing
topics.keywords: bus transit route cuts frequency trimet train max
topics.body: TriMet staff and Board of Directors
topics.authority: TriMet operates regional transit. Its Board sets agency policy; its general manager oversees operations under that policy. Portland City Council does not run TriMet.
topics.process: Use TriMet’s public meeting materials to identify the specific proposal and decision maker. Board meetings include public input; confirm the current sign-up instructions before participating.

decisions.title: Property rights for Stark & Washington safety work
decisions.proposal: Allow the city to acquire property rights needed for planned safety improvements along SE Stark and SE Washington.
decisions.change: The proposal would authorize acquisition, including eminent-domain proceedings if needed. It does not establish that construction is finished. The impact statement says the planned project cannot proceed without the necessary rights.
decisions.meetingLabel: Council session starts at 2 p.m. Pacific; item time may change.
decisions.deadlineLabel: Virtual testimony registration closes one hour before the session. This is not the written-comment deadline.
decisions.participation: Check whether testimony is available for this item on the official agenda. In-person sign-up is before the item is heard. Written testimony is generally accepted before Council votes; check for item-specific changes.

decisions.title: Extend a nonprofit housing tax exemption
decisions.proposal: Update the city code for the nonprofit low-income housing property tax exemption.
decisions.change: The current city code lists a January 1, 2027 sunset. The proposal aligns it with July 1, 2033 and revises program procedures. Eligibility is not determined by this app.
